text:
elaine: FYI, after flipping on compression + adding the trace headers to the OTLP exporter we started seeing intermittent 5xx from the collector. Happening on gRPC streaming only. logs attached (short extracts below).

raj: which exporter (service/config) and protocol — gRPC or HTTP?

elaine: gRPC streaming to collector in us-west. Config snippet:```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/grpc:
    endpoint: collector.redwood.local:4317
    compression: gzip
    headers:
      traceparent: "{{traceparent}}"
    timeout: 10s
    retry_on_failure: true
```

sam: streaming + compression + some proxies (envoy/nginx) can lead to partial flushes or buffer pressure. Also gzipped streaming frames sometimes trip proxy heuristics. Try disabling `compression` to see if that drops errors.

marta: also consider idempotency. If the collector retries a non-idempotent unary/streaming call, backend might reject duplicates. Do we attach any request id header?

elaine: no request id at the moment. The collector has no consistent id header so retries look identical. Error samples: `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed` and occasional `resource exhausted`.

observability-bot: Alert: otlp-exporter-errors rate spike -> 3.7% (5m window) for service=ingest-otlp at 2026-03-16T10:12:34Z

raj: quick checklist: 1) disable compression 2) add an `otlp-req-id` header (uuid per root flow) 3) set retry policy with idempotency awareness 4) tune timeouts/backoff

sam: example change I usually apply for gRPC streaming:```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/grpc:
    compression: none
    headers:
      otlp-req-id: "{{workflow_id}}-{{span_count}}"
    keepalive:
      time: 30s
      permit_without_stream: true
    max_concurrent_streams: 200
    timeout: 15s
    retry_on_failure: true
    retry_settings:
      max_retries: 3
      initial_backoff: 100ms
      max_backoff: 2s
      multiplier: 2.0
```

marta: if we can't rely on proxies, fallback policy to HTTP/protobuf is useful — unary HTTP is more proxy-friendly. Also add a circuit-breaker: if >1% 5xx for 5m then route new exporters to http endpoint and mark gRPC as degraded in console.

elaine: I spun a canary: disabled compression + added otlp-req-id header. Errors dropped to ~0.6% in canary vs 3.7% prod. Switched to HTTP/protobuf for a second canary and saw 0.2% error rate.

deploy-bot: rolled export-config changes to canary cluster (canary-otlp) by elaine at 2026-03-16T10:25:00Z

raj: sounds like two orthogonal issues: (A) compression+streaming vs proxies (B) missing idempotency/request ids for safe retries. Both worth addressing. Proposal: short-term patch = disable compression + add `otlp-req-id` + conservative retries/timeouts. Medium-term = implement automated routing/fallback policy (gRPC -> HTTP) and add UI control in console to opt fallback thresholds.

sam: plus we should tune collector settings: `max_concurrent_streams` and grpc keepalive to prevent `resource exhausted` under bursts. And add synthetic tests that exercise large-batch streaming through our proxy.

marta: I'll draft the fallback/circuit-break RFC for the console UX: threshold configuration, automated route, and an audit log for switches. Include migration notes for dedicated/private customers.

elaine: I'll put together a short test plan and the canary comparison numbers, then open a PR with the exporter config change. Will also add a short script to generate `otlp-req-id` in the SDKs.

raj: great. Can we also add a dashboard tile to show exporter error rate by protocol + compression flag so SREs can triage quickly?

elaine: yes — adding a per-protocol error breakdown to the ingester dashboard. Will add a query and a small note in the runbook.

sam: TL;DR: disable gzip for streaming over unknown proxies, add request-id for idempotency, tune timeouts/backoff, and add automated gRPC->HTTP fallback with console controls.

elaine: thanks team — I'll file the RFC/PRs and ping y'all. :thumbsup:
